text: B.  Google vs Apple — what differs
Same OIDC flow, different details in the id_token and the secret.

// decoded id_token payload
{
  "iss": "https://appleid.apple.com",
  "aud": "com.example.app",
  "sub": "001234.ab12cd...0987",
  "email": "x7k2@privaterelay.appleid.com",
  "is_private_email": true,
  "email_verified": true,
  "nonce_supported": true,
  "auth_time": 1767225590,
  "exp": 1767229200
}

Keys (JWKS):  googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/certs
Algorithm:    RS256
client_secret: a static string
Name + email: sent on every login
Scopes:       openid email profile
Callback:     GET (query string)

Keys (JWKS):  appleid.apple.com/auth/keys
Algorithm:    RS256
client_secret: ES256 JWT you sign (.p8 key)
Name + email: ONLY on first login!
Scopes:       name email
Callback:     POST (form_post)

Store name/email immediately — Apple never
sends them again. Email may be a private relay.
Rules that apply to BOTH providers

1.  Verify the id_token on your server — signature, iss, aud, exp, nonce.
2.  Match state (CSRF) and nonce (replay) from step 2.
3.  Identify users by (iss, sub) — never by email alone.
4.  Use PKCE even with a backend; mandatory for SPA / mobile.
5.  Exchange the code server-side so client_secret stays secret.
6.  Then mint YOUR OWN short-lived JWTs — don't reuse the provider's
     access_token as your session.
